To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the X-ray fluxes at which the HS state begins and the HS state flux peak are correlated, and (b) this correlation holds up to a timescale of ∼104 d, which is comparable to the viscous timescale at ∼104–105Rg.
the correlation between the transition flux and the flux peak of HS state is still valid after the source reaches the flux peak of the HS state.
the correlation between the transition flux and the flux peak in the following high/soft state of SXTs extends up to 250 d after the transition.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the physical processes of the accretion flows during the state transitions of SXTs, and the results are important for understanding the accretion processes of the accreting black hole and neutron stars in the LH-to-HSS state transitions.
the correlation between the flux at which the LH-to-Hs state transition occurs and that at the HS flux peak, and the correlation time scales.
a new aspect of the correlation between the fluxes of the two states of LMXBs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mass accreting flow in the LH-to-HX transition region is correlated on a viscous timescale, which is much larger than the dynamical timescale.

the X-ray flux correlation is due to the correlation between the accretion rate and the viscosity in a two-flow geometry, which is the result of the interaction between a sub-Keplarian outflow and a Keplerian inflow in the accreted material.
the X-ray fluxes of the accretion disk in SXTs correlate over a large region in the disk and over a long time scale.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the mass acccretion rate at a given radius is positively correlated with that at other radii at the same time, or the mass accreted at a given radius over a long period is correlated with that over the same period at other radii.
the accretion rate in the disk flow, either the total mass accretion rate or the mass accretions rate at a given radius, correlates with the X-ray flux in the HS state.
the accretion rate in the disk is the key factor for the state transition and the subsequent evolution of the X-ray light curves.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the correlation timescale between the transition and the peak flux is not a constant for all the sources and it is likely related to the viscous timescale in the accretions flow.
the accretion rates of the two flow geometry in the LH and HS state are closely related to the state transition.
the X-ray fluxes of SXTs are correlated over a long timescale, which can be used to constrain the accretion disk structure and the physical processes of SXTs.
